texts.orig: 1 The Big Picture
texts.text: 1 The Big Picture

texts.label: text
texts.orig: For the rest of the term you will build one thing in three steps: a small file-transfer service, the Eagle Transfer Protocol (ETP), and the network stack underneath it.
texts.text: For the rest of the term you will build one thing in three steps: a small file-transfer service, the Eagle Transfer Protocol (ETP), and the network stack underneath it.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: PA1 - the application over TCP. You implement the ETP/1 server and client from a written specification, the way real protocols are implemented: from an RFC. Your server serves many clients at once and survives the ones that misbehave. Then you capture your own session on the wire and explain, segment by segment, what TCP did with your bytes.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: PA2 - a reliable transport over UDP. UDP loses, duplicates and reorders. You build ETP-T, a small reliable byte stream on top of it - sequence numbers, acknowledgments, a checksum, a retransmission timer and a sliding window - and you measure it through a relay that drops, delays and reorders your datagrams.
texts.text: PA2 - a reliable transport over UDP. UDP loses, duplicates and reorders. You build ETP-T, a small reliable byte stream on top of it - sequence numbers, acknowledgments, a checksum, a retransmission timer and a sliding window - and you measure it through a relay that drops, delays and reorders your datagrams.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: The Final Project - your stack, end to end. With a partner, you put the PA1 application on top of the PA2 transport, add one extension, and measure the result against TCP under the same conditions. You report what you found in writing and in a short video.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: ETP-T carries a byte stream over UDP with sequence numbers, cumulative acknowledgments, an Internet checksum (Chapter 5, §5.3.2), a retransmission timer and a sliding window (§5.4). You will run it through an instructor-supplied lossy relay - a small program that sits between your sender and receiver and drops, delays and reorders datagrams - using a random seed assigned to you, and measure throughput against window size and loss rate, comparing it with the stop-and-wait bound.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: With your partner you put the ETP/1 application on ETP-T through the seam, choose one extension, and measure your stack against TCP under identical relay conditions. The extension menu will include Go-Back-N versus Selective Repeat, AIMD congestion control, a connection handshake and teardown, a multi-client server over ETP-T, and confidentiality and integrity with authenticated encryption (AES-GCM).

texts.text: This section applies to every milestone. Each brief names that milestone's core. For packet captures and measurements in this project, this section replaces the syllabus's "tool syntax only" rule for packet-analysis write-ups.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: You may use generative AI tools in this project. Working engineers do, and learning to use them well is part of what this course should teach you. But the point of these assignments is that you learn network programming: how a byte stream behaves, how framing works, how a server survives its clients, how reliability is built from loss. A tool that does that thinking for you takes the learning with it, and the final exam, the project, and your first job will find the gap.

texts.orig: Everything you build here runs on loopback or inside your Lab 0 virtual machine. Capture only your own loopback traffic. Do not point your client, your server, the relay or a capture at any other host or network. The syllabus's Hands-On Activity Scope and Authorization rules apply in full. Use synthetic data - random bytes or files you made - never real credentials or personal data.
